calls.reason: The Nature Medicine study backs the doctor point but covers older models and one task. The short-story study gives mixed signals on writing, and there is no accounting evidence. Too thin to call all three.

The Danish study found about 3% time savings and no effect on earnings or hours. The ILO says full automation is limited, and Anthropic's own data shows no whole jobs automated. Together they point to little real automation.

Salesforce's claims are self-reported and not specific to entry level. SignalFire names several causes, and the freelance novice decline is indirect. That falls short of proof, but the record is mixed and the search was not exhaustive.

Salesforce's hiring freeze is the company's own claim, and the 20% drop in freelance coding demand is suggestive but not role replacement. The Danish study found minimal effects. The evidence is mixed.
An opinionated claim about media behaviour. Two articles (CIO, MacRumors) cut both ways, and there is no representative media sample or evidence about what journalists understand.

A forecast with no deadline. The Commonwealth Bank reversal and Careerminds' rehiring figures fit the prediction but do not show the same workers returning after LLM failures, and Klarna's cuts came through attrition.
